clue.text: Financial institution put out after last borrower showed lack of assets

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing loosely for an adjective meaning unable to pay debts

indicators.note: after places the shuffled put behind the borrower's final letter

parts.note: a bank is the standard financial institution

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word borrower
out signals that the letters of put are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A bank turned away a customer who had no assets to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the three letters of 'put', and 'after' sets them behind the last letter of 'borrower'. The definition reads loosely: one who showed a lack of assets was ruined financially.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to pay creditors because one's assets have run out is the legal state of insolvency.

clue.text: Bachelor fires off legal rulings

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of fires go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bachelor angrily fires off a batch of court judgments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fires off' looks like a phrase for sending something quickly; 'off' is really the anagram signal acting on 'fires'.
explanation.definitionFit: In law the documents setting out a case for counsel carry this name, used loosely here for legal decisions.

clue.text: The restoration on Vermeer will not take place at any future time

definitions.text: will not take place at any future time

indicators.note: restoration of a painting suggests its parts being remade, so the letters of on and Vermeer are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restorer is told the work on a Vermeer painting will never happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The restoration' rearranges ON VERMEER into the nine letters of the answer; the art-restoration picture hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a literary adverb meaning never again, the raven's refrain in Poe's poem.

clue.text: First rate meal cooked in the country

indicators.note: First picks out the opening letter of the word rate
cooked suggests the letters of meal being mixed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A first-rate meal was prepared in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First rate' reads as one praising phrase, but 'First' takes the opening letter of 'rate' and 'cooked' rearranges 'meal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or domain is a synonym for a nation or land.

clue.text: The era of contraception in the sack?

indicators.note: era of contraception puts the contraceptive word ahead of the era word in the answer

parts.note: the Pill is the common name for oral contraception
an age is an era or period of history

explanation.surface: A question about the time when the contraceptive pill arrived, set in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The era of contraception' gives PILL AGE in answer order. 'sack' reads as bed (in the sack), but means plunder as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder and loot it.

clue.text: Here in France the first three clematis were frozen solid

parts.note: ici is French for here

indicators.note: the first three asks for just the opening three letters of clematis

explanation.surface: In France the first three clematis plants were killed by frost.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI (French 'here') plus CLE, the first three letters of 'clematis'. The definition is loose: a noun for something that has frozen solid; 'were' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of ice forms when dripping water freezes hard.

clue.text: Official will order girl into the vehicle

indicators.note: into tells us the order and girl go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat commands a young woman to get into the car.
explanation.walkthrough: OM (Order of Merit, a British honour) and MISS go 'into' CAR. 'will order' looks like a command but 'order' is a noun giving OM; 'will' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissar was a Communist Party functionary in the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Plants do in Guernsey and Sark

indicators.note: in tells us do sits inside the islands' abbreviation

parts.note: both are Channel Islands, abbreviated CI
to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: The plants doing well on two of the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Guernsey and Sark are two of the Channel Islands, between England and France. 'do' looks like a verb about thriving; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These spiny desert succulents are plants of the family Cactaceae.

clue.text: Feeling of sickness? No question, it's a facility

indicators.note: No here means without, so the question abbreviation is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: queasiness is a feeling of nausea

explanation.surface: Someone feeling sick insists, without a doubt, that it is a mere convenience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' drops QU (abbreviation for question) from QUEASINESS. 'No question' reads as 'certainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility means ease or lack of difficulty, as in doing something with facility.

clue.text: Sailor held in vile surroundings is incapable of surviving

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: held shows the sailor kept inside something else
surroundings says the word vile wraps round the sailor

parts.note: taken as written
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is kept in squalid conditions where nobody could live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' and 'surroundings' together signal the container: the sailor sits inside 'vile', making a word for able to live, and 'in' stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes an organism or plan that cannot live or succeed.

clue.text: Shifts the honeycombs

definitions.meaning: shifts are loose, simple dresses or overgarments
as a verb, to decorate fabric with a honeycomb pattern of gathered stitches

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifts' is not a verb here but a noun for loose garments; 'honeycombs' is a needlework verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The garments are loose overalls; the verb means to gather cloth with smocking, a honeycomb stitch.

clue.text: Always include attempt at climbing exercises

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters are read upwards
include puts the attempt inside always

parts.note: ay is an old word for always
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Keep trying to climb as part of a fitness routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' makes AGOY, which 'climbing' turns upwards, as a down answer is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu discipline is practised as a set of postures and breathing routines.

clue.text: Diplomats at strange meeting place

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, home of British diplomats
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Diplomats gather at an odd venue.
explanation.walkthrough: FO (the Foreign Office, Britain's diplomatic service) plus RUM, old British slang for odd; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome this was the public square where citizens met and debated.

clue.text: A throwback, one turning into a suppressive act

parts.note: a lob is a high throw; taken back it reads backwards
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: turning shows the letters of into twisted round into a new order

explanation.surface: A primitive throwback turns into an oppressive measure.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then LOB reversed (the 'throwback'), I, and INTO 'turning' to TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing away with a practice or law by decree, as with slavery, is an act of putting it down.

clue.text: Where to get Ecus to pay for our involvement in mad cow disease?

definitions.text: Where to get Ecus to pay for

indicators.note: involvement in places our inside the disease's abbreviation

parts.note: BSE, bovine spongiform encephalopathy, is mad cow disease
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks where Europe can find money to cover its part in the BSE crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Mad cow disease was a 1990s British cattle crisis. The Ecu was the European currency unit before the euro; 'involvement in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental stock exchange, as in Paris, is where money is raised.

clue.text: Do they sell kits to help blind mice?

definitions.text: Do they sell kits to help blind mice?

parts.words: Do they sell kits to help blind mice?
parts.note: shopkeepers seen as people who would give tails back to the three blind mice of the nursery rhyme, whose tails were cut off

explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme 'Three Blind Mice' the farmer's wife cuts off their tails; split as RE-TAILERS, the answer would restore them.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers who sell goods to the public are the people the clue asks about.

clue.text: Helps when it's stormy on board

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: on board conventionally means put inside the ship's SS

parts.note: a steamship, abbreviated SS, is the board one is on

indicators.note: stormy suggests the letters of it's tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lending a hand when the weather turns rough on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: AS, then IST ('it's' rearranged by 'stormy') put 'on board' SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Assists are aids or supports, also a sports term for passes that help a goal.

clue.text: Food that fills up spaces give it the treatment

indicators.note: give the treatment suggests working the letters over into a new order

parts.note: gaps are spaces

explanation.surface: A dish that crams every gap, given the full works.
explanation.walkthrough: GAPS (for 'spaces') with IT and THE are rearranged as 'give it the treatment' says; 'that fills up' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strings of pasta are an Italian staple food.

clue.text: A man's man?

parts.note: a Man's man is a native of the Isle of Man, not a macho type

explanation.walkthrough: 'a man's man' usually means a manly fellow; the capital M would point to the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman lives on an island, so he is an inhabitant of one.

clue.text: One who shows it is a very warm jersey

definitions.text: One who shows it is a very warm
definitions.meaning: a person who perspires shows that it is hot
a jersey is a knitted pullover

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: someone who perspires.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a perspiring person and a woollen pullover share the name.

clue.text: Regrets the streets of Paris

definitions.meaning: to regret is to be sorry about
French for streets, plural of the word on Parisian street signs

explanation.definitionFit: The English verb means feels sorry about, and the French noun means roads in a town.

clue.text: Office desk

definitions.meaning: an agency or department, such as a travel agency

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a government department and a writing desk with drawers.

clue.text: To invest in a worker is retrograde for example

indicators.note: in places the reversed is and the example inside the worker

parts.note: a bee is a worker insect

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word is reads in reverse

explanation.surface: Putting money into a worker is a backward step, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrograde' turns 'is' to SI; 'in' places that and EG within the worker. 'invest' reads as finance but has its old military sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town is the old military sense: to surround it with troops.

clue.text: Revolutionary Green Party finally showed vigour

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters of green are rearranged
finally picks out the closing letter of party

explanation.surface: A radical Green Party ended up showing real drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' rearranges GREEN to ENERG, and Y is the last letter of 'Party'; 'showed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour is strength and vitality, the capacity for vigorous activity.

clue.text: Sprays a cat which rises awkwardly

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of rises are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat sprays as it clambers up clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: A, TOM (male cat), then RISES rearranged by 'awkwardly' to ISERS; 'which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices that turn liquid into a fine spray, such as perfume bottles.

clue.text: Hate the stage of being without parking

indicators.note: without means the parking letter is taken away

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform or stage
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Disliking the stage of life when there is nowhere to park.
explanation.walkthrough: PODIUM without P (parking); 'of being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is intense hatred or general disgust.

clue.text: Like a layer of white

parts.note: as means like, as in as good as gold
a hen is a layer of eggs

explanation.surface: Something resembling a coat of white paint.
explanation.walkthrough: AS plus HEN: 'a layer' looks like a coating, but it is a bird that lays eggs. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour of ash: pale grey, as of a face drained of colour.

clue.text: Farewell to cube in gold

indicators.note: in places the cube within gold's symbol

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a small cube used in games

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to a cube made of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: DIE (one of a pair of dice) inside AU, gold's symbol; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A French goodbye borrowed into English, said when parting for a long time.

clue.text: Chauffered physician and archdeacon around the island

indicators.note: around shows the doctor and archdeacon going round the island

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
Ven, Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A doctor and an archdeacon were driven round the island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venerable is the formal title of an archdeacon in the Church of England. The clue misspells chauffeured.
explanation.definitionFit: To be chauffeured is to be taken somewhere by car by a hired driver.

clue.text: The king, for example, tries to organise a list

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king

indicators.note: to organise means the letters of tries are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The king, for instance, attempts to draw up a list.
explanation.walkthrough: R (Rex, king) plus EG, then TRIES rearranged by 'to organise' to ISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An official record of names, such as a class roll.

clue.text: Misers can be negligent

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of misers could become another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Misers are capable of being careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges MISERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careless in one's duties is a synonym for negligence.

clue.text: Pledge to cruise round the outskirts of Torbay

indicators.note: round suggests the letters of cruise turned about into a new order
the outskirts of picks the first and last letters of Torbay

explanation.surface: A promise of a cruise around the edge of a Devon resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges 'cruise' to SECURI, and 'the outskirts of' takes the first and last letters of Torbay, an English seaside resort in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral, something given as a guarantee for a loan, is a pledge.
